---
title: "El Niño"
description: "ENSO conditions and Southwest climate"
---

ENSO tends to have its clearest Southwest precipitation relationship during
the October-March cool season. El Niño years are often wetter and La Niña
years often drier, but individual years can differ sharply across Arizona and
New Mexico. [CLIMAS explains the regional pattern](https://climas.arizona.edu/sw-climate/enso-and-monsoon).

The historical archive pilot compares two completed seasons:

- [Water year 1998](archive/wy1998.qmd) (DJF RONI +2.1 °C)
- [Water year 2011](archive/wy2011.qmd) (DJF RONI -1.4 °C)

Each page has six cool-season maps and two full-water-year context maps. The
RONI values use the December-February [NOAA Relative Oceanic Niño Index](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso/roni/).
The maps show observed conditions, not changes caused solely by ENSO.
